title: Oil-bulk-ore carrier Khoryv sinks off Romania, one dead and three missing
excerpt: The Comoros-flagged ship was hit by a drone about 13 nautical miles off Constanța on 23 October; nine crew were rescued.
x_post: The Comoros-flagged oil-bulk-ore carrier Khoryv sank after a drone strike off Romania on 23 October, killing one and leaving three missing, Romania's naval authority said. #MaritimeSecurity #Shipping #Seafarers #BlackSea

lesson (facts): A ship on fire in one sea is not the same attack as a ship disabled in another: merge two unnamed reports only when a so
notes: The Cape Dao is not an attack of 26 October. She was struck on 23 September, one seafarer was killed, and she sank about 35 nautical miles east of Sohar on 14 October after salvage failed, as Lloyd's List reported on 26 October when she was declared a total loss. If she is mentioned at all, use those dates, that place and that death.

Keep the vessel on fire off Iraq as its own Persian Gulf item. UKMTO warning 183-26 reported it 63 nautical miles southeast of Al-Faw on 26 October from multiple third party reports, with the name, cause and crew status unknown, so do not credit Iran with it and do not call it a sinking.

The tanker of UKMTO warning 182-26 was struck at 0839 UTC on 23 October and UKMTO disclosed it on 26 October. Call her a tanker, never a bulk carrier, give her no name, do not say she sank, and say the report came three days late.

The Khoryv is an oil-bulk-ore carrier (VesselFinder, IMO 8138712), not a general cargo ship. Use that type in the headline, standfirst, lede, key points, her paragraph and the tweet, keep the headline at 80 characters or fewer, and keep one dead and three missing in the headline and lede.
